follow_up_note: The linked follow-up verifies native ClamAV CLI and MCP stdio progress, timeout, cancellation, checkpoint contents and resume using local synthetic files. The original automated-test scope below is unchanged.
tested_changes: Uncommitted long-running scan progress implementation and regression tests

implementation.cli: Malware scans report initial, one-second and final progress to stderr; stdout remains one JSON report
implementation.counters: Batch targets, not individual files or estimated percentages; unknown values remain null. Partial observations may also remain pending for retry
implementation.saved_parts: Number of records in the last successfully replaced checkpoint, including prior records awaiting revalidation. A failed write retains the previous successful saved count
implementation.cancellation: First CLI Ctrl+C requests graceful cancellation; the second interrupts. MCP cancellation requests worker shutdown and checkpoint preservation
implementation.mcp: State changes are notified at most once per second, with ten-second heartbeats; numeric progress is elapsed seconds with no estimated total
implementation.post_cancel_query: get_scan_progress reads eventual state by scan_id or the latest request. Final cancellation notification is best effort because SDK callbacks can be removed before worker completion
implementation.retention: Latest 32 request states in server memory; lost on restart, independent of durable batch checkpoints
implementation.privacy: Progress contains no file names, findings or history contents
implementation.classification: Timeout and cancellation stages use the monotonic deadline and cancellation event, not warning text

coverage: Cancellation after a completed part preserves one saved part and one pending part
CLI stderr progress leaves stdout as a single JSON report
MCP final and intermediate progress carries actual counts and monotonic elapsed time
Checkpoint write failure distinguishes observed results from successfully saved results
Actual child-process timeout preserves checkpoint counts
Actual CLI SIGINT stops the engine child, returns partial, and reports saved counts
Actual MCP cancellation permits querying eventual saved state
Untrusted warning text cannot forge a timeout stage
Ordinary scans report one target and no applicable checkpoint
Progress retention is bounded and missing IDs return an error
Notification failure does not lose the scan or checkpoint

limitations: Tests use synthetic data and controlled engine subprocesses; a home scan with actual ClamAV was not repeated
Native Windows Ctrl+C behavior and Windows CI were not executed here
MCP client UI rendering was not manually verified; SDK and npm stdio protocol behavior were tested
